1. If water is still flowing from the toilet:
   - Find the shutoff valve behind or beside the toilet (near the wall) and turn it clockwise until the water stops.
   - If you can’t find it or it doesn’t work, turn off the **main** water supply to your home (usually in a basement, utility room, or outside near the street).

2. Electrical/safety:
   - If water is near electrical outlets, cords, or appliances, **do not** step into the water. Stay back and, if safe to do so, turn off power to that area at the breaker.

3. Limit damage:
   - Use towels or a mop to keep water from spreading to other rooms if it’s safe to be on the floor.
   - Move any rugs, boxes, or electronics out of the wet area.

To help you find emergency plumbing, tell me:
- Your city and ZIP code
- Whether you’re in a house or an apartment
- Is the toilet still actively overflowing, or has it stopped once you shut off the water?

Once I have that, I’ll check what emergency options exist in your area and explain what can and can’t be arranged from here.</action>

<action type="say">
Here’s a focused checklist you can use when they arrive:

1. Cause and scope
- “Can you show me what caused the overflow?”
- “Is this just a blockage at this toilet, or could it be an issue in the main sewer line?”
- “Did you check the main cleanout or only this fixture?”

2. What they’re doing today
- “Exactly what work are you planning to do to fix this?”
- “Will you pull the toilet, snake the line, or both?”

3. Costs
- “Can you give me an itemized estimate before you start—service call fee, labor, parts, and any emergency/after‑hours fees?”
- “Is that a flat rate or could it go higher? Under what circumstances?”

4. Testing before they leave
- “Before you go, can we flush several times and run the sink/shower to be sure everything drains normally and won’t back up again?”

5. Condition of the toilet and pipes
- “Is this toilet in good condition, or are any parts worn (fill valve, flush valve, wax ring) that you recommend replacing now?”
- “Do you see any signs that my pipes or main line are older or at risk of future problems?”

6. Warranty and follow‑up
- “If this toilet backs up again soon, what’s your callback or warranty policy?”
- “Will I get the details in writing (invoice/receipt) with what work you did today?”

Before they arrive, it helps to:
- Clear everything away from around the toilet so they can work.
- Keep a couple of old towels and a trash bag handy, in case they need to pull the toilet.

If you share what they say the cause is and the estimate they give, I can help you sanity‑check it.</action>
